uncited: This family encompasses methods that utilize neural networks to solve the inverse problem of tomographic reconstruction, either by serving as implicit regularizers, direct mapping functions, or feature extractors within a differentiable rendering loop.
Unlike traditional algebraic or analytical methods, these approaches leverage the expressive power of deep learning to handle sparse, noisy, or incomplete projection data.

They distinguish themselves from sibling methods like [Neural Adaptive Tomography (NeAT)](1862-neural-adaptive-tomography-neat.md) by focusing on end-to-end differentiable architectures or implicit priors rather than explicit adaptive sampling or specific Gaussian parameterizations.
**Backward Projection (Adjoint):** Distributing the error from the 2D detector plane back into the 3D volume.
Processing: $r$ passes through Embedding Conv 2D and U-net Blocks. $z$ is processed by a 'Modified Block' (described in Section 2.2 of source, not detailed here) and integrated into the network.
Sample M points p_m on ray r with depths t_m. 2.
Calculate relative depth encoding E_m for each point using δ_m. 3.
Element-wise add E_m to point feature f_m. 4.
Pass through self-attention and feed-forward network to predict volume density σ_m.
The application of deep learning to tomographic reconstruction has evolved from post-processing denoising to end-to-end differentiable inverse rendering.
Early works focused on using CNNs to clean FBP reconstructions, while recent approaches integrate neural networks directly into the forward model to learn complex priors or implicit representations.
